title: Zealandia separates from Gondwana
summary: Zealandia, a 4.9 million square kilometre region of continental crust in the southwest Pacific, was once part of Gondwana. The GSA Today paper describes a continental breakup unconformity of about 84 Ma, and NASA says New Zealand's land mass separated from Gondwana around 80 million years ago.

uncertainty.note: Start is the ca. 84 Ma breakup unconformity in Mortimer et al. (2017); end is NASA's around 80 million years ago. Other published ranges for the separation differ and no opened page gives a single date. The 2 Ma allowances are not sourced.

as_recorded.value: a widespread continental breakup unconformity of ca. 84 Ma age
separated from the ancient supercontinent of Gondwana around 80 million years ago

where.modern_name: Zealandia, southwest Pacific Ocean (including New Zealand and New Caledonia)
where.historical_name: Eastern margin of Gondwana (no polities exist at this date)

paleo.plate_model: MULLER2019 (Muller et al. 2019, Tectonics) via GPlates Web Service
paleo.note: Point -40, 170 reconstructed to 84 Ma. MERDITH2021 gives -66.69, -167.35 and PALEOMAP -65.32, 175.98: the models agree on about 63-67 S but differ in longitude. Indicative only.

importance.justification: Zealandia is argued to be a mostly submerged continent, 94% under water.
